newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Yahoo! eyes Asian opportunities.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Yahoo! eyes Asian opportunities.

text.p: Online Internet guide Yahoo! Inc is looking to Asia for opportunities to expand, and could set up a presence outside Japan within six to 12 months, said chief Jerry Yang on Friday.

"One of the main reasons I'm here is to understand a little better what opportunities are here...what kind of activities (Asia's) having on the Internet and who's getting on the Internet and what kind of content is being developed," Yang, a co-founder of Yahoo!, told Reuters in an interview.

He said international expansion was key to the U.S.-based company's growth. Yahoo! has joint ventures in Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Canada to provide sites tailored for users in those countries.
Australia would probably be the next place for Yahoo to enter, but Asia was a high priority, he said.

"We might want to do something targeted towards the English speaking/reading population, something like a mirror site, basically duplicating what we have in the States here in a local server, so people can have better access, faster access -- an Asian server," he said.
This could happen within six to 12 months. Later Yahoo! would look to providing information in Asian languages, he said.
"We would try to do what we've done in other regions, which is to collect information that's specific to this area but also allow them to access the global database," he said.
Yahoo also has to figure out how to sell advertising -- which would be its prime revenue generator -- in Asia.
"Right now the opportunities we believe are really in the advertising area. The Internet media is very much like other media, such as television and radio," which rely on advertising.
An estimated one percent of total U.S. advertising spending, or about US$2.0 billion, would be allocated to the Internet by 2000, he said. Yahoo! had 230 advertisers in June.

"The Asian advertising market is a developing market...and we're catching it at the right place," he said. "We can probably get an even higher percentage as...(advertising) budgets increase over time."
Yang said Yahoo! identifed itself not as a technology or software firm, but as a media company, which people are gradually viewing as an information service.
"From a media standpoint, we are very much differentiated...not just a search and directory, a lot of news, a lot of stock quotes."
"Stock quotes alone are now doing more than one million page queries a day," he said.
Yahoo! has 1.5 million to 2 million users per day, and about 300 million pages viewed per month.

He said the company's strengths included developing regional content. In the U.S., Yahoo! has launched sites for metropolitan areas like San Francisco and Los Angeles. Yahoo! is also aggressively developing personalised information services.
"If people always think of Yahoo! when they need to find information - that's our goal," said Yang.
He said in the longer term, the Internet could sustain two to three prominent players who use the same approach of being content providers through branding and advertising.
"I think we will be among the two or three," he said.
